claim: adding drops, xp, crops and mobs to the fixture exposed the dominant real cost: 667ms per tick, 72 percent in the drop stage, caused by an O(n^2) merge loop
why: slice 18 rejected the remaining membership hoists because the fixture had no drops, xp, crops or mobs, so their cost was invisible
measurement: same runner and release build, 3 processes, 100 warmup and 1000 measured ticks per scenario. entity_heavy: 600 drops, 600 xp, 600 crops, 600 mobs = 667ms per tick, drops 72 percent, environment 27 percent. entity_heavy_furnaces adds 400 active furnaces = 674ms.
significance: 667ms per tick would break a 20TPS server outright. This was completely invisible in every previous fixture.
cause: drop_tick merges same-item nearby drops with a nested loop over all pairs, about 180000 pairs per tick at 600 drops. dp[i].comps == dp[j].comps is evaluated before the cheap distance test.
fix_plan: bucket by integer cell and only compare the own cell plus its 26 neighbours, since a distance under 0.5 implies the floors differ by at most one on each axis. To stay equivalent, iterate i in original order, collect candidate j from the neighbourhood, filter to j > i, sort ascending, and merge on the first match.
not_equivalent: sorting the drops and comparing neighbours changes which drop is absorbed, so that approach is rejected
status: fixture added only. drop_tick is unchanged.
tests: 32 passed, 0 failed, 1 explicitly ignored, serial and at 8 threads
review: NOT RUN, external usage limit still in force
